thread.title: Asian markets tumble, following tech losses on Wall Street

author: Dow Jones Newswires
title: Asian markets tumble, following tech losses on Wall Street
text:
Asian stock markets saw volatile trading Tuesday following Monday’s rout, led by tech stocks, on Wall Street.
Every sector in Japan’s stock market turned lower as the Nikkei NIK, -2.06% dropped more than 2%. Investors were quick to react to the U.S. losses, especially among suppliers linked to Apple’s AAPL, -5.04% iPhone. TDK 6762, -6.27% and Murata 6981, -4.76% were all down sharply. Meanwhile, SoftBank 9984, +1.87% rose 1.8%, making up an early 4% loss, following its after-the-bell update on the planned IPO for its Japanese mobile unit . Japanese auto companies Toyota 7203, -2.44% and Honda 7267, -2.19% fell after reports hit saying the Trump administration is planning tariffs on auto imports.
Bucking an earlier sharper drop, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index HSI, +0.62% rose 0.6%, with energy stocks weak given oil’s sharp reversal, with CNOOC 0883, -3.06% falling 3%.
Mainland China stocks fared better, with the Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, +0.93% managing a gain of nearly 1% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite 399106, +1.63% up 1.6%. Still, iPhone component suppliers Secote Precision 603283, -1.15% and Luxshare 002475, -1.85% both lower.
Benchmark indexes in South Korea SEU, -0.44% and Taiwan Y9999, -0.56% dropped modestly, weighed down by tech names. Samsung 005930, -1.55% fell almost 2% and SK Hynix 000660, -3.49% plummeted 3.5%, while Taiwan Semiconductor 2330, -1.73% was off 1.7%.
Australia’s ASX 200 XJO, -1.80% closed down 1.8%, as energy and financial names dropped, and New Zealand stocks NZ50GR, -1.06% eased about 1%.
